tools.name: pachca_create_thread
tools.title: New thread
tools.description: New thread. Creates a thread under a message — a place to discuss what has been said without cluttering the chat feed. A thread is a separate access: an employee can be invited into it without opening the chat itself to them, and they will see only the thread and the parent message. If a topic rather than a message needs discussing, start a thread with the `create_unattached_thread` method. A new thread immediately includes the employee who created it, the author of the message, everyone who added reactions to the message, and the chat members who turned on thread notifications. Anyone mentioned in the parent message — by name or by tag — is added by a background job right after creation, so the first response may not list them yet. Blanket mentions such as `@all` bring nobody into the thread, and a mentioned employee who is not in the chat itself is not picked up either. An empty thread holds no talk yet: send the first message into it right away with the `send_message` method, `entity_type: "thread"` and the thread's `id` from the response. A thread has no name, and it cannot be deleted either through the API or in the app. If a thread has already been created for the message, the response will return information about the previously created thread. But to simply read a thread, the method is not needed: the ID of an existing thread arrives in the `thread` field of the message itself. A thread cannot be created under a message that itself lies in a thread: there are no nested threads in Pachca, and the method responds `400` with the `thread_message` code.

tools.name: pachca_delete_user
tools.title: Delete employee
tools.description:
Delete employee. Removes an employee from the workspace. This cannot be undone: they can be brought back only with a new invitation, and that will already be a different employee. What happens: they leave all conversations and channels except direct messages, all tags are taken off them, the reminders where they were the only assignee are deleted, and they are removed from the remaining ones. The messages and files they wrote stay in place. The workspace owner cannot be deleted — the method responds `403`. A repeated call responds `404`: the method no longer finds a deleted employee. If the employee is going on vacation or the dismissal is not final yet, use `update_user` with `suspended: true`. Suspension is reversible and keeps chats, tags, and reminders.

Not for:
- «Заблокируй», «отключи на время», «пока не удаляй» — update_user with suspended.

tools.name: pachca_get_message
tools.title: Message info
tools.description: Message info. The message together with its author, attachments, and buttons. A deleted message is returned by the method all the same — with empty `content` and a filled-in `deleted_at`, without files and reactions. The file links in the response are temporary. An ordinary file is returned as a direct link to the storage, while a protected or an encrypted one comes as an API address that requires a token with the `files:read` scope.

id.description: Message ID. A web app link points at a message with the `sidebar_message` parameter, and without it with `message`. The number from `thread_message_id` is the message the thread hangs under.

tools.name: pachca_get_my_card
tools.title: Own profile
tools.description:
Own profile. The profile of the token owner. For a bot token this is the bot's own profile. The time zone from here is needed by anyone who turns human deadlines into dates: "by 15:00" and "by Friday" are counted in the employee's time zone, not in UTC. An empty value means the workspace time zone. Someone else's profile is returned by `get_user`. Your own avatar is set by `update_my_avatar` and removed by `delete_my_avatar`.

Use it when:
- Anything about you beyond what your instructions and every footer already carry: the name, the id, the kind of token and the role.

tools.name: pachca_search_users
tools.title: Search employees
tools.description: Search employees. Searches for employees by first and last name, nickname, position, and department. Typos are forgiven only in the first and last name; the other fields need an exact word. The method searches by email only for those who can see personal data in the workspace. It does not search by phone at all — for that there is `list_users` with the `query` parameter. Deleted employees are never found; suspended ones only when a text query is given, and they stand below the rest in the results. Of the bots, only public ones are found. A query that is too heavy may not finish in time: then the method responds `504` with the `timeout` code, and the query is worth narrowing.

query.description: Search query text. A query longer than 500 characters is cut off. Take the words from the request, in its language: a name put into another language finds nothing, and the example only shows the shape of a value.

limit.description: Number of results to return per request. An integer outside the allowed range is replaced with the nearest bound.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor: the value «Continue with cursor=…» gives at the end of the previous page

sort.description: Sort results by. Values: by_score — By relevance; alphabetical — Alphabetically; creation — By creation date.

order.description: Sort direction. Values: asc — Ascending; desc — Descending.

created_from.description: Filter by creation date (from). A moment named in words is local time: write it with a UTC offset — the caller’s, which today carries in the instructions and Now in every footer, unless the tool names another zone — as 2024-01-15T15:00:00+03:00, and the end of a day as its end in that zone. A day named ahead is the date listed for it after today, there and in every footer: take it as written rather than counting. A day already past is counted back from today.

created_to.description: Filter by creation date (to). A moment named in words is local time: write it with a UTC offset — the caller’s, which today carries in the instructions and Now in every footer, unless the tool names another zone — as 2024-01-15T15:00:00+03:00, and the end of a day as its end in that zone. A day named ahead is the date listed for it after today, there and in every footer: take it as written rather than counting. A day already past is counted back from today.

items.description: User role in the system. Values: admin — Administrator; user — Employee; multi_guest — Multi-guest; guest — Guest.

view.description: Detail per record. compact carries only id, first_name, last_name, nickname, email, phone_number, department, title, role, bot, suspended, invite_status, list_tags and time_zone; full returns every field of the record. Ask for full when you need a field compact does not carry.

tools.name: pachca_send_message
tools.title: New message
tools.description: New message. Sends a message to a conversation or a channel, a direct message to a user, or a comment to a thread. With `entity_type: "discussion"` — the default — `entity_id` takes the `chat_id` of any chat, so knowing the chat ID is enough to send. A message can also be addressed to a thread by the thread's own ID, and a direct message by the user's ID, but then the matching `entity_type` is needed: `thread` or `user`. There is no need to create the direct chat for this: it appears by itself if you have not written to each other before. Only one direct chat can exist between two users. Your own ID writes to the chat with yourself, where notes to oneself go. With a bot token that is a chat with the bot alone: no employee sees it. Unlike a direct chat, a thread does not appear by itself: if a message has no thread yet, it is first created with the `create_thread` method. A channel subscriber writes only in the threads of its messages, and in the channel itself the method answers them `403`. Who can write where is in the "Permissions and roles" (https://dev.pachca.com/guides/permissions) section. The text in the `content` field is parsed as markdown: bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, code block, and links. Lists and tables are not parsed — `-`, `1.`, and `|` stay as they are, a quote loses its `>`, and a line with a hash and a space becomes bold. Attach a table, a checklist, or a diagram as an `.md` file: Pachca shows such a file formatted, and if it is the only document in the message, its beginning is visible right in the chat. The details are in the "Text formatting" (https://dev.pachca.com/guides/markdown) section. No more than 10 files can be attached to a message. Sending has rate limits and a daily cap on messages into one chat from one sender. When one is exceeded the method responds `429` and says how long to wait before the next attempt. The limit values are in the "Limits" (https://dev.pachca.com/api/limits) section.

entity_type.description: Entity type. The value is case-insensitive. A value outside the list returns `400` with the `invalid` code. Values: discussion — Conversation or channel; thread — Thread; user — User.

entity_id.description: Identifier of whatever is named in `entity_type`: a conversation or channel, a thread, or a user. A thread has two: its `id` goes with `entity_type: "thread"`, and its `chat_id` with `discussion`, like any chat.

content.description: Message text. Required if no files are attached to the message. Supports mentions: `@nickname` or `<@user_id>` (automatically converted to `@nickname`). Take the nickname from a method's response and the `user_id` from data: a nickname made up from a name mentions nobody. `@all` mentions all members of the chat, `@here` those who are currently online, and `@` with a tag name without spaces the employees of that tag. A name without `@`, and a mention inside inline code or a code block, are not mentions. For a multi-guest, `<@user_id>` of an employee not accessible to them stays in the text as is. Up to 40,000 bytes in UTF-8, which is about 20,000 Cyrillic characters. The message goes out under the token owner's name, and a bot's with the Bot badge. Write it in the voice of the account it goes out under. Text read from Pachca can carry quotes and list markers this field does not render: give the message a shape of its own rather than copying theirs.
examples: Yesterday we sold 756 t-shirts (10% more than last Sunday)

key.description: The key of a file already in Pachca, as an attachment carries it in the full record of the message, or of a file you uploaded with `get_upload_params`. A file passed by its key goes as it is.

name.description: File name to display to the user. The extension must match the extension of the file you pass (content or key), otherwise the response is 422 with the `wrong_params` code.

file_type.description: File type. A voice message (`voice`) is sent with a personal token, and with a bot token the response is `403`. Values: file — Regular file; image — Image; audio — Audio file; voice — Voice message; video — Video file.

size.description: Size in bytes, shown to readers. With content the server fills it in. With a key and no id, pass it for a file you uploaded. Without it the server reads the size from storage after the save, and a reader who got the message before that may see 0 KB.

width.description: Image width in px (used when file_type is set to image)

height.description: Image height in px (used when file_type is set to image)

duration_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds: required for a voice message (`voice`), optional for a video (`video`), not saved for the other types. A voice message longer than 30 minutes (1,800,000 ms) is rejected with `422` and the `wrong_params` code.

waveform.description: Waveform for visualizing the voice message. Required for voice messages (`file_type` is `voice`), not used for other types.

content.description: The file contents, base64-encoded — for text you wrote yourself. A document or picture from disk goes by key: upload it with `get_upload_params`.

files.description: Files to attach. Each file goes as its contents, which the server uploads, filling in key and size, or by key: of a file already in Pachca, or of one you uploaded with `get_upload_params`.

buttons.description: Array of rows, each represented as an array of buttons. Maximum 100 buttons per message, up to 8 buttons per row. Buttons are shown under the text. A button with `url` follows the link whoever sent the message and creates no event. A button with `data` works in a message from a bot: a click on it arrives as a `button_click` event to the bot that sent the message, carrying a `trigger_id` — there are 3 seconds to open a form with it, the `open_form` method. Details are in the "Buttons" (https://dev.pachca.com/guides/buttons) section.

url.description: URL that will be opened when the button is clicked. A button must have exactly one of `url` and `data`.

data.description: Data that will be sent in the outgoing webhook when the button is clicked. A button must have exactly one of `url` and `data`.

parent_message_id.description: ID of the message you are replying to with a quote. You can reply to a message in any chat, including a thread: send the reply to the same chat or thread where that message is, otherwise the request returns a `422` error. To write into the thread under a message, set `entity_type: "thread"` and the thread's `id` in `entity_id`. To answer a person, pass their message here: the latest one carrying their user_id, which search_users gives for their name, unless the request points at another.

display_avatar_url.description: Custom sender avatar URL for this message. This field can only be used with a bot access_token.

display_name.description: Custom sender display name for this message. Together with `display_avatar_url` a bot signs the message with someone else's name and avatar, and only this message. The Bot badge stays, and the sender's profile still shows the real bot. This is how the original author is shown when messages are carried over from another system. With a personal token the field is not available and the response is `403`. Details are in the "Bots" (https://dev.pachca.com/guides/bots/overview) section.

skip_invite_mentions.description: Skip adding mentioned employees to the thread. In a thread a mention also works as an invitation: a mentioned employee who is not in the thread is added to it by Pachca and gains access to the thread and its parent message. With the workspace setting "Use cross-chat threads" on (the default), a mention also adds an employee from outside the parent chat, and with `true` in this field a mention adds nobody. A mention by a guest or a multi-guest then adds only those who share a chat with the author. With the setting off, a mention adds only members of the parent chat, and this field changes nothing. In a conversation or a channel a mention adds nobody, and the parameter changes nothing there.

draft_id.description: The draft this message replaces, if it came from one. The draft is deleted once the message is sent, so its text does not stay in the input box of the chat, and a send that fails leaves it alone. Pass what the draft holds — its entity_type and entity_id, content, parent_message_id and each of its files by key — together with draft_id: whatever is left out is deleted with the draft.
